thread:
Alex P: kicking off CLE GPU cluster provisioning (cle-gpu-3). Network attachments are up but I want a quick sanity sweep before we mark this ready for smoke. Key checks: routing through the transit GW, peering prefix visibility, NAT egress behavior from GPU nodes, DNS delegation for cle.redwood.internal, and immediate bandwidth/cost risk. tagging @net-eng and @infra-oncall — ETA ~2h for full validation.

Marta L: on it — running route table + BGP dumps now, will paste findings.

Chong: pasted route table diff: ```
RouteTable rt-08abc123
- 10.200.0.0/16 -> local
- 10.201.0.0/16 -> tgw-attach-0
+ missing route for 10.202.0.0/16 -> should be via tgw-attach-2
```
Looks like the GPU subnet (10.202.0.0/16) hasn't been propagated to the transit attachment for CLE. That explains asymmetry when we tried an outbound test earlier. :eyes:

infra-bot: automated-net-checks: transit-attachment CLE-TGW-02: BGP sessions UP (2/2). Advertised prefixes: 10.200.0.0/16,10.201.0.0/16. Learned prefixes from downstream: 172.31.0.0/16. WARNING: 10.202.0.0/16 not advertised. NAT egress check: pending — no external IP observed from sample GPU instance.

Jess (oncall): can we confirm whether GPU nodes are on the right route table / ENI? also we need to know if NAT uses ephemeral EIPs or a pool — cost implications if something starts doing cross-region egress.

Alex P: Chong/Marta can you confirm which account attachment owns 10.202? I think the subnet was added late in the provisioning script and may not have been pushed to the TGW route table. For cost: we should assume $0.09/GB egress baseline for planning, but cross-region would be higher. Let's add a temporary bandwidth alert at 200GB/day for this cluster.

Marta L: found it — the cle-gpu-3 subnet was created under the new VPC (vpc-cle-gpu-3) but we forgot to call the tgw-propagate job. Quick fix: ```
aws ec2 create-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-id tgw-0abcd --vpc-id vpc-cle-gpu-3 --subnet-ids subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb
# then run: infractl tgw propagate --vpc vpc-cle-gpu-3
```
I'll run those commands and recheck routes.

Chong: FYI when you run propagate, watch for BGP dampening on the partner edge — we had a flapping session last month that caused prefixes to be suppressed. Also add `community:no-export` to internal-only prefixes so they don't leak to partners.

infra-bot: update: transit-attachment propagation complete. Learned prefixes now include 10.202.0.0/16. NAT check: GPU instance src 10.202.12.7 -> egress EIP 3.120.45.22, external connect to httpbin.org succeeded.

Jess (oncall): great. Now DNS — I tried resolving the controlplane VIP from on-prem and got NXDOMAIN. Did we create the delegation in onprem DNS and the glue records in the registrar?

Alex P: DNS was supposed to be delegated to ns1/2.cle.redwood.internal. Marta — did the automation push the zone?

Marta L: deployment created the Route53 private zone `cle.redwood.internal` and stack outputs include `ns1.cle.redwood.internal (10.3.4.5)`. However, on-prem DNS team needs the forwarder config. I pinged them (cc @net-eng) and they say they need the delegation IPs added. I can add a temporary forwarding zone in our onprem forwarders to avoid block.

Chong: temporary workaround: point the onprem resolvers at our VPC resolver IP (10.3.4.5) or add an A glue record at registrar if the zone needs to be public. For internal-only we should prefer forwarder.

Jess (oncall): cost note — if onprem can't resolve and apps fall back to internet paths, we'll risk cross-region egress and higher charges. Also set a throttle alert on the NAT gateway — create CloudWatch alarm: `NatGatewayBytesOut > 200GB in 24h` -> notify #finance-alerts and #eng-infra.

Alex P: agreed. Marta, after you finish propagate + DNS forwarding, run the smoke test: 1) curl metadata and verify controlplane access 2) run a simple training microjob to validate sustained egress and GPU node health 3) confirm autoscaler can attach nodes to vpc-cle-gpu-3. Post results here and then we can mark ready for the formal handoff doc.

Marta L: will do. quick smoke commands I'm running: ```
curl -sS http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/local-ipv4
dig @10.3.4.5 controlplane.cle.redwood.internal A +short
kubectl --context cle-gpu-3 get nodes -o wide
stress-ng --matrix 0 --timeout 60s # quick GPU job
```
Posting outputs in ~10m. :thumbsup:

Alex P: thanks — if all green I'll open the handoff thread and attach the runbook PR (network changes, NAT policy, DNS delegation steps, and a short cost estimate). tagging @eng-sre for final smoke later.

infra-bot: final status snapshot: routes propagated, NAT egress functional, DNS delegation pending onprem forwarder change. Next action: Marta to coordinate forwarder update and create cost alert.

Chong: note for runbook: include exact `aws ec2` commands, expected route-table IDs, and a small troubleshooting section for BGP suppression and flapping. saved me 2hrs last time.

Jess (oncall): I'll be available for the handoff in 1.5h window. if any red flags ping me. :white_check_mark:

Alex P: closing loop — thanks team. I'll wait for Marta's outputs and then draft the handoff doc.
